w10_T4_002883: A pack of 20 stickers was shared equally among 4 children, and Ola kept her share. Her aunt then gave her 16 more stickers, and she used 12 stickers on her homework folder. At the school shop every sticker can be swapped for 4 tokens, and Ola swapped all of hers. The swap took her about a quarter of an hour, fifteen minutes. How many tokens does Ola have?
w10_T4_002886: Jonas picked 23 bags of pears in the morning and 24 bags after lunch, with 3 pears in every bag. He tipped them all into a crate and added 36 loose pears from the ground. At the market he sold 154 pears, then his cousin Ana, whose crate held fewer pears than his, gave him 37 pears she could not sell. Each pear weighs about 200 grams. How many pears are in Jonas's crate now?
w10_T4_002892: In the morning Mira had 82 marbles in her bag, and she won 44 more at recess. In the afternoon she gave half of her marbles to her brother. In the evening at the toy swap she traded every marble she had left for 4 beads each, and then gave 124 of the beads to her cousin. How many beads does Mira have?
w10_T4_002893: In the morning a drinks depot had 166 crates of lemonade, and a lorry delivered 72 more crates. In the afternoon the crates were unpacked: each held 8 bottles, all of which went onto the shelves. In the evening 67 loose bottles were added from a returned order, and then 66 more from another. How many bottles were on the shelves at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002896: A nursery sowed 20 trays of lavender, each tray having 9 rows with 3 seedlings in every row. It sold 271 seedlings in the spring. From every seedling that was left, the gardener took 6 cuttings, and a friend gave her 67 cuttings from his own plants. The greenhouse is 12 metres long. How many cuttings does the gardener have?
w10_T4_002900: In the morning Kai loaded 154 crates of granola bars onto his truck, then squeezed in 3 more crates. Every crate holds 7 boxes, every box holds 5 packs, and every pack holds 7 bars. The truck is 12 metres long. In the afternoon he collected 47 loose bars from a sample stand and added them to the load. In the evening he counted the whole load bar by bar; his colleague Lu's truck carried fewer bars. How many bars were on Kai's truck?
w10_T4_002913: Ben saved 26 dollars a week for 7 weeks in one envelope, then added 79 dollars from his birthday. He keeps his savings in dollars, knowing a hundred cents make a dollar. At the arcade he changed every dollar in the envelope into 3 tokens. The arcade has 40 machines. The machines only take strips of 3 tokens, so he had all his tokens bundled into strips of 3. He used 189 strips over the afternoon. How many strips does Ben have left?
w10_T4_002925: In the morning the bakery shelf held 163 loaves. By noon 106 loaves had been sold, and in the afternoon 51 more went, over a stretch of one hundred and eighty minutes, that is, three hours. Then 1 loaf fell and was thrown away. In the evening 5 fresh loaves were put on the shelf. How many loaves were on the shelf at the end of the evening?
w10_T4_002927: Priya sold 37 bracelets a day for 9 days at the craft market, then sold 64 more at a school fair. Each bracelet sold for 9 dollars, and she also received 40 dollars in tips. Her stall is 2 metres wide, and she offers a dozen different designs. At the bank she changed all of her money into quarters, 4 quarters to a dollar, since a dollar is one hundred cents. How many quarters did Priya get?
w10_T4_002929: In the morning the church donation box held 75 dollars, and a visitor added 36 dollars. In the afternoon a wedding party put in 55 dollars and a passer-by added 32 dollars. In the evening the treasurer took 150 dollars out of the box to pay the electricity bill. How many dollars were left in the donation box?
w10_T4_002932: A school has 170 students, but 95 of them are away on a trip. Each student still at school is given 5 worksheets. By the end of the day 303 worksheets have been completed and handed in. Each worksheet not yet handed in has 4 pages, and every page has 7 problems. The school has 8 classrooms. How many problems remain on the worksheets not yet handed in?
w10_T4_002933: A bakery baked 144 trays of rolls with 6 rolls on each tray, and added 15 rolls left from yesterday. The rolls were divided equally among its 3 delivery vans, which are painted in 2 colours. The driver of the first van sold every roll in his van at 3 dollars each and was also handed a 35-dollar tip. How many dollars did the first van's driver collect?
w10_T4_002935: The knitting club's 82 members each knitted 9 squares for a charity blanket, and half of them stayed late to sew. A local shop gave 51 ready-made squares as well. Every square takes 7 metres of yarn, and the club measures its yarn in metres although a thousand metres make a kilometre. Of all the yarn used, 1973 metres had been donated free; the rest was bought. The club meets on the 3rd Tuesday of every month. How many metres of yarn did the club have to buy?
w10_T4_002936: Sofia's coin jar held 198 coins. She spent 179 coins at the arcade and lost 9 coins on the bus. Her father then gave her 33 coins, and she found 65 coins in an old coat. Her friend Luis has fewer coins in his jar than Sofia. How many coins are in Sofia's jar now?
w10_T4_002942: Tariq planted 22 chilli seeds, but 21 of them never came up. He bought 64 young chilli plants from the garden centre and was given 41 more by his neighbour Nadia, who has fewer plants than Tariq. A dozen weeks later, every one of his plants produced 9 chillies. How many chillies did Tariq's plants produce?
w10_T4_002944: In the morning a florist unpacked 175 bunches of tulips, with 6 stems in each bunch, into one big display, then added 45 loose stems. In the afternoon she sold 298 stems, and 7 stems snapped and were discarded. In the evening a hotel bought every stem left in the display at 8 dollars each; the florist prices in dollars, knowing a hundred cents make a dollar. How many dollars did the hotel pay?
w10_T4_002947: A coach company owns 31 coaches, but 13 are in the workshop this week. Each working coach runs 4 trips a day, each trip lasting ninety minutes, an hour and a half, and this continued for 6 days. The company also ran 71 extra trips for a festival. Every coach seats 50 passengers. Of all the trips that week, 436 were fully booked. How many trips were not fully booked?
w10_T4_002949: In the morning 158 visitors entered the museum before nine o'clock, followed by 10 more from a coach party and 59 from a school. In the afternoon 5 art students and then 62 tourists came in, guided by a dozen volunteers. In the evening 25 guests arrived for a lecture that lasted ninety minutes, an hour and a half. How many visitors entered the museum that day?
w10_T4_002951: A baker sent 150 cupcakes to the school fair, shared equally among 5 stalls. At the first stall, 2 of the cupcakes were eaten by the helpers. The rest were cut into 4 quarters each for tasting, and the quarters were packed 4 to a box. The fair ran for 3 days. Every box sold for 6 dollars, and the stall priced things in dollars even though a hundred cents make a dollar. How many dollars did the first stall make from the boxes?
w10_T4_002954: A club bought 151 balloons for the hall, which is 20 metres long. While inflating them, 37 balloons popped, and 84 were given away to children at the door. The remaining balloons were tied into 6 equal bunches. From the bunch by the stage, 2 balloons floated away. How many balloons were left in the bunch by the stage?
w10_T4_002957: Aria went to the fair with 112 dollars and spent 32 dollars on the entrance ticket. She changed all her remaining dollars into ride tokens at 5 tokens per dollar, but the rides were closed, so she changed all the tokens back into dollars at the same rate of 5 tokens per dollar. She won 27 dollars at a raffle and then paid 96 dollars for a giant teddy bear. She counts in dollars, though she knows a hundred cents make a dollar. Her friend Bo went home with less money than Aria. How many dollars did Aria have when she went home?
w10_T4_002958: In the morning a wholesaler unloaded 234 crates of oranges, each crate holding 9 boxes with 8 oranges in every box. In the afternoon 1500 oranges went to a juice bar and 14602 to a supermarket. The wholesaler's lorry is 15 metres long. In the evening every orange still in the warehouse was sold to a street vendor at 9 cents apiece. How many cents did the street vendor pay?
w10_T4_002960: In the morning a printing press produced 233 sheets an hour for 5 hours, three hundred minutes of running, and 82 of the sheets were smudged and thrown away. In the afternoon every good sheet was cut into 3 posters. Then 1163 posters were sent to a cinema. In the evening 1843 posters were sent to a concert promoter. How many posters were left at the print shop?
w10_T4_002964: Tom had 32 pairs of socks, with 2 socks in each pair, all loose in one drawer. He put 51 socks in the wash and lost 4 socks behind the machine. His mother then bought him 30 socks, and his grandmother sent 76 more, all of which went into the drawer. The drawer has 3 compartments. How many socks are in Tom's drawer now?
w10_T4_002970: In the first week of training Nina ran 33 minutes a day. In the second week she doubled her daily time and kept that up for all 7 days of the week. Her coach did not count 89 of those second-week minutes because they were warm-up, but he added 17 minutes for a time trial. Her teammate Eli was credited with fewer minutes than Nina for that week. How many minutes was Nina credited with for the second week?
